column1: # session + ui + screen batch (evidence-backed rows only)
# --- session: every name below is pinned by the peer that talks to it ---
# GameClient: b()/c() are the player count and the name array the lobby screen displays (written by
#   the STATUS branch from the server's slot list) -> getPlayerCount/getPlayerNames ;
#   a(GameEventListener) is the per-frame pump that drains received commands, ticks the simulator and
#   returns whether the server is RUNNING -> update ; d() prunes chat older than 20s and returns the
#   accumulated text -> getChatText ; a(int) sends SLOTS (slot index + user name) -> claimSlot ;
#   a(boolean) sends READY -> setReady ; a(GameCommand) sends COMMAND (used by NetworkedUnitCommander
#   for every order) -> sendCommand ; f() is the local Player behind NetworkedUnitCommander.getPlayer
#   -> getPlayer ; g() is "reader thread alive" -> isConnected ; j() dials the socket -> connect ;
# GameServer: c() is the tick body invoked by ServerTickThread (drain commands, broadcast state, run
#   three 33ms simulator steps) -> tick ; a(GameCommand) fans a command out to all clients and queues
#   it locally -> broadcastCommand ; a(String) fans a chat line out -> broadcast ; b() clears the
#   accept-loop thread -> stop ; a(World,int) builds the "4|name, n/m Players, k Teams, type" match
#   label -> buildMatchLabel ; d() is the "mm:ss: " uptime stamp used as the log prefix
#   -> getLogPrefix. The synthetics forward to those very members (a->lock, b->sessions,
#   c->getLogPrefix, d->clients, e->world, f->state, g->tick thread, h->tick and the three setters).
# ServerClientSession: a(Object) enqueues a message for ClientWriterThread -> send ; a() is "reader
#   thread alive" -> isOpen ; b() is "open and the client said READY" -> isReady ; c() is "open and
#   the client's STATUS flag is set" -> isPlaying ; d() is the player name used in every log line
#   -> getPlayerName ; e() stops the reader loop (called by GameServer's shutdown) -> stop ;
#   g() closes writer/reader/socket -> close. The synthetics expose writer thread, send batch,
#   pending queue, writer and server to the two helper threads.
# Modes: TutorialGameMode/TestScenarioMode.d() is what restoreStartWorld() calls to rebuild the
#   scenario world from its .world file -> createStartWorld. Their empty e()/f() hooks carry no
#   evidence and stay unnamed, as does CampaignGameMode.p() (evidence: it is "lite mode or Mac
#   build" gating the mission subset, but no call-site name is forced).
# Label.a(int) delegates to setColor(int) - i.e. the class already has that semantic name, which is
# why RenameAst's collision check rejects it. It is a leftover delegating accessor and stays as is.
# ScriptStep.d() / TutorialHintBox.b() are the same script column: GameScreen parses it as a command
# GuiAssets accessors, named from where they are consumed:
#   j() -> the four content insets BaseMenuScreen applies around a dialog nine-patch
#   r() -> the ButtonStyle BaseMenuScreen.createButton builds every dialog button with
#   w()/x() -> the item and selection styles BaseMenuScreen.createListBox passes to ListBox
#   y() -> the big nine-patch behind menu panels (MainMenuScreen/CampaignScreen/SkirmishSetupScreen)
#   z() -> the nine-patch behind the FullScreen option row in MainMenuScreen -> getOptionRowNinePatch
#   t() -> the 55px row strip used above buttons in the menu/dialog lists -> getRowNinePatch
#   u() -> the 196x51 region drawn on that strip -> getRowHighlightRegion
#   s() -> the nine-patch behind the difficulty list in CampaignScreen -> getListPanelNinePatch
#   A()/B()/C() -> the three assets GameScreen hands to the TutorialHintBox constructor
# SelectionPanelBase.a(String,ZZZZZZ) is left unnamed: it switches four sub-panels by six booleans
#   whose meaning is not decidable from the body alone.
# BaseScreen.y() forwards to GameApplication.resetCursor() and is called after a display-mode change
# CampaignScreen.j() clears the mission container and rebuilds the mission buttons from the campaign
#   mode -> rebuildMissionList ; k() resets the campaign and rebuilds -> resetCampaign.
# GameScene.a()/b(): b() is the flag the input code checks as "a panel/dialog owns the input"
#   (if (!t.b()) ...), a() is true exactly for the five map scenes f..j -> isPanelOpen / isMapScene.
# GameScreen.r(GameScreen)/a(GameScreen,long) are the nanos clock the listeners read
#   (onGameTick stores it; BuildPanelListener compares and advances it by 1e9) -> getGameTimeNanos /
